“The fourth mountain had many plants. They were green at the top and dry near the roots. Some had also withered in the sun. Some of its believers have divided allegiance. Others have the Lord on their lips, but not in their hearts.”

2. “Their foundations are dry and powerless. Their words alone are alive. Their works are dead. They are neither alive nor dead.[a] They resemble people of divided allegiance. Those people are neither green nor dry, neither alive nor dead.”

3. “Their plants withered when they saw the sun. In the same way, people of divided allegiance hear of persecution. Out of cowardice, they worship idols and are ashamed of their Lord’s name.”

4. “They are neither alive nor dead.[b] But if they repent quickly, they too can live. If they do not repent,[c] they have already been handed over to the women who take away their life.”

translation:
  text: '“The believers from the fourth mountain are like this. It had many plants, green at the top but
    dry near the roots, some also withered by the sun. Some of these believers are people of divided allegiance;
    others have the Lord on their lips but not in their hearts.”


    2. “That is why their foundations are dry and powerless. Only their words are alive; their works are
    dead. Such people are neither alive nor dead.[a] They resemble those of divided allegiance, for people
    of divided allegiance are neither green nor dry; they are neither alive nor dead.”


    3. “Just as their plants withered when they saw the sun, so people of divided allegiance worship idols
    out of cowardice when they hear of persecution, and are ashamed of their Lord’s name.”


    4. “Such people, then, are neither alive nor dead.[b] Yet if they repent quickly, they too can live.
    But if they do not repent,[c] they have already been handed over to the women who take away their
    life.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The first “neither alive nor dead” sentence in paragraph2 follows Anger’s printed insertion
      compared with the two Latin traditions and Ethiopic; Athos is reported to omit it. Later in this
      paragraph Athos reverses the green/dry order. The draft retains the printed order and the repeated
      life/death contrast.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Alive nor” in paragraph4 is inserted by Anger compared with the Latin traditions and Ethiopic;
      the reported Athos text lacks it, leaving “Such people, then, have not died.” This supplement is
      distinct from the similar insertion in paragraph2.
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Can live. But if they do not repent” is Hilgenfeld’s insertion, compared with the Latin traditions
      and Ethiopic and attributed in the apparatus to an omission by similar endings in Athos. Without
      it: “Yet even these people, if they repent quickly, have already been handed over to the women who
      take away their life.” The draft retains the printed repair but does not claim the whole condition
      is directly surviving Greek. P.Oxy.3528 does not cover this paragraph.'
